title: Boston September 1 Move-Out: Getting Rid of Furniture and Mattresses
meta_description: Moving out of a Boston apartment on Sept 1? City rules for curbside furniture, mattress and fridge appointments, plus donation pickups that book weeks ahead.
h1: Moving out of a Boston apartment on September 1: how to get rid of furniture
options_h: Every option we list for a Boston move-out: 11 ways to clear out furniture, mattresses and appliances
intro: The City of Boston says most leases in Boston turn over at the beginning of September. If you're moving out, the City's rules are: furniture can go out with your trash on your regular collection day, mattresses and box springs need a free pickup appointment, and TVs, air conditioners and fridges need a special pickup through 311. Nothing on this page is a guess: each rule below is quoted from the City's pages or the organization's own site.

quick_answers.q: Can I leave furniture on the curb when I move out in Boston?
quick_answers.a: Yes, on your scheduled collection day, and the City page doesn't mention a fee. The City says household furniture can be put out with your normal curbside trash and recycling on your collection day, by 6 a.m. or after 5 p.m. the night before, placed along the curb so the sidewalk stays clear. The City strongly encourages donating it instead.

quick_answers.q: Can I put a mattress out on the curb on September 1 in Boston?
quick_answers.a: Not without an appointment. Because of the Massachusetts mattress disposal ban, Boston no longer collects mattresses or box springs with regular trash. You must book a free curbside pickup at boston.gov/mattress; the City program only serves buildings with six units or fewer.

quick_answers.q: How do I get rid of a fridge, TV or air conditioner when moving out of Boston?
quick_answers.a: Book a City special item pickup through 311 or online. The City does not collect special items without an appointment, takes at most 5 items per appointment and 10 per calendar year, and won't take a fridge or freezer unless the doors are removed and the food is out.

quick_answers.q: I live in a building with 7 or more units. Who takes my mattress?
quick_answers.a: Not the City's mattress program. The City says residents of buildings with seven or more units should ask their property manager how to recycle a mattress; private mattress haulers are another option.

quick_answers.q: How far ahead should I book a donation pickup for September 1?
quick_answers.a: It depends on the organization. Household Goods says its volunteer pickups are typically scheduled four or more weeks ahead, while its paid partners can come in as soon as two business days, and ReSupply's Boston page lists priority pickups in 24 to 48 hours. Other donation pickups don't state a lead time.

sections.h: What the City says about the September move-in period
sections.p: Ahead of the 2026 move-in period, the City said its Public Works Code Enforcement Division issues citations for improper storage of household trash, and asked residents to put trash and recycling on the curb by 6 a.m. on collection day or after 5 p.m. the night before. It also asked residents not to block sidewalks or curb ramps with trash or furniture: items should go along the curb, leaving room for pedestrians, including people with disabilities and people pushing strollers. The City's moving page notes that most leases in Boston turn over at the beginning of September.

sections.h: Will Boston trash pick up furniture on move-out day?
sections.p: Yes, if it's your regular collection day. The City says furniture can be put out with your normal curbside trash and recycling on your scheduled collection day; in large residential buildings it should be placed neatly next to the trash receptacles. Check your day in the City's Trash Day app or schedule search. The City does not collect construction debris, plumbing fixtures, water heaters, fences, or auto parts; dishwashers and large exercise equipment go to donation or a private hauler.

sections.h: Mattresses and box springs: book the City pickup first
sections.p: The City will not collect any mattress or box spring without an appointment. Book a free curbside pickup online; the program covers buildings with six units or fewer, and residents of buildings with seven or more units must check with their property manager. Put the mattress on the curb by 6 a.m. on the appointment day or after 5 p.m. the night before. Cancellations must be made before 12 p.m. the day before, and a missed pickup must be reported to 311 within 24 hours of the scheduled date.

sections.h: Fridges, TVs and air conditioners: special pickup by appointment
sections.p: The City collects refrigerators, freezers, air conditioners, dehumidifiers, TVs, computer monitors and laptops only by appointment, through 311 or online. Place the item where trash is collected (curbside, public alley or dumpster area), not on private property. Remove all fridge and freezer doors, including on mini fridges, and all food, or the item won't be taken. Don't smash appliances or electronics, wipe data from computers, and set TVs and computers out freestanding rather than boxed. The limit is 5 items per appointment and 10 per calendar year.

sections.h: Donate before you move: book ahead
sections.p: The City strongly encourages donating furniture rather than putting it out. Pickup lead times vary: Household Goods says its volunteer pickups (only in Acton and eight nearby towns, not Boston) are typically scheduled four or more weeks ahead, and Boston donors can drop off in Acton or use its paid pickup partners, which can come in as soon as two business days. ReSupply, the paid pickup service Habitat Greater Boston and Household Goods point donors to, lists priority pickups in 24 to 48 hours. Furnishing Hope picks up only donations of at least six substantial furniture items and asks for photos before scheduling. The Habitat ReStore in West Roxbury takes drop-offs Tuesday through Saturday, 9:30 a.m. to 4 p.m.

sources.label: ReSupply: Where can you donate furniture in Boston?

sections.p: If a curbside day or appointment doesn't fit your lease end, paid services will come inside. LoadUp's national page lists full-service removal from $75 and same-day pickup in most areas, and ReSupply's Boston page lists prices starting at $99 for sofas and bulky furniture plus a booking fee. Prices are starting prices from their own pages; confirm a quote for your address.
